instruction: Wire brush, scraper, angle grinder with cup wheel
Industrial vacuum / blower, water jet
Long-nap roller, stiff brush, airless sprayer (optional)
Slow-speed drill mixer (400–600 rpm), stiff nylon brush, trowel
Primer roller, cutter, hand roller / pressure roller, measuring tape
Cutter, chalk line, hand roller, hot-air welder (HS15S)
Slow-speed mixer, notched squeegee, short-nap roller, wet-film gauge
Moisture meter, crack-width gauge, measuring tape
qa_check: Crack gauge and moisture meter available

instruction: Wear safety helmet, safety shoes, nitrile gloves and safety goggles.
qa_check: PPE checked for every crew member

instruction: Use full-body harness and lifelines on terraces and facades above 2 m.
Solvent-based primer: no naked flames, ensure ventilation, store away from heat.
Use organic vapour mask in closed areas; ensure cross-ventilation.
Keep MSDS / safety sheet on site; barricade the work zone.
Remove dust, laitance, oil, loose mortar and old failed coatings by scraping / grinding.
qa_check: Surface sound and free of contaminants

instruction: Grind sharp edges; form 25 × 25 mm cement-polymer coving at wall–floor junctions.
qa_check: Coving provided at all internal corners

instruction: Pre-wet the surface to saturated-surface-dry (SSD) – no standing water.
qa_check: Surface SSD at time of application

instruction: Surface must be dry: moisture content below 5% (moisture meter).
Surface must be fully dry (moisture < 4%) and primed if porous.
Surface dry, smooth and free of sharp projections that could puncture the membrane.
Blinding / shoring face level and smooth; voids filled; no standing water.
Dewater the excavation; keep groundwater below working level until backfill.
Measure crack width and depth with the crack gauge; mark on drawing.
Hairline (< 0.3 mm): brush-in an extra stripe coat of the waterproofing material.
Fine to medium (0.3–3 mm): open into 6 × 6 mm V-groove, clean and fill with polymer crack filler.
Structural (> 3 mm) or live cracks: refer to structural engineer before waterproofing.
Apply APS1 bitumen primer by roller at ~40 sq ft/L; allow to become touch-dry.
Apply a diluted first coat (1 : 1 with water) as a primer coat.
No separate primer – SSD substrate acts as primer for cementitious coats.
Apply recommended primer on porous concrete before PU (illustrative).
No primer required for pre-applied HDPE.
Stir well; apply by roller / brush in cross direction to the previous coat.
Mix Part A and Part B with slow-speed mixer for 3 min to a lump-free slurry; use within 45 min.
Apply first coat by stiff brush; second coat at right angles once the first is touch-dry.
qa_check: Coats at right angles; no pinholes

instruction: Unroll membrane, align, peel release film and press down from centre outwards.
Provide 75 mm side laps and 100 mm end laps; roll laps firmly; seal with DST where specified.
Lay HDPE with membrane face towards concrete; 75 mm selvedge laps taped / welded.
Protect membrane from rebar chairs and foot traffic; pour concrete within 30 days.
Apply PU with squeegee / roller to the specified wet-film thickness; second coat crosswise.
Embed fibre mesh 150 mm wide at corners, upstands, drains and pipe penetrations in the first coat.
qa_check: Mesh fully embedded – no exposed fibres

instruction: Turn waterproofing up 300 mm on parapets / walls (150 mm in bathrooms) and terminate in a groove.
Seal around rainwater outlets and pipes with a collar of mesh + extra coat.
Allow to air-dry. Protect from rain for 24 h; full cure in ~7 days.
Moist-cure by light water spray / wet hessian for 3 days; avoid direct sun.
Allow to cure undisturbed; no foot traffic for 24 h; full cure in ~7 days.
No curing needed; protect membrane from UV and traffic until the protection layer is placed.
No curing needed; protect from UV beyond 30 days and from site traffic.
48-hour flood / ponding test with 50 mm of water after full cure; check soffit for damp patches.
qa_check: Ponding test passed – no damp below

instruction: 48-hour ponding test before placing protection screed; check soffit.
48-hour ponding test with 25–50 mm water; check ceiling below before tiling.
48-hour ponding test; inspect the slab underside and adjoining walls.
Fill tank to full level for 7 days after curing; mark and check water level daily.
Fill pool in stages over 7 days; monitor level and balancing tank before tiling.
Visual inspection + cross-cut adhesion check on a test patch; water-spray test on a sample bay.
Visual inspection of every lap and penetration; spark / vacuum test on suspicious areas (illustrative).
Visual inspection of laps and terminations before rebar placement; record photos.
Visual inspection of laps; check drainage board outlets before backfill.
Visual check; water-spray test across the joint after full cure.
Place the protection layer (screed / board / tiles) as specified without damaging the waterproofing.
qa_check: Protection layer in place – no punctures

instruction: Clean the area, remove debris and hand over with a signed test report.
Issue as-built photos, batch numbers of materials used and warranty documentation.
Brief the owner / facility team on dos and don'ts (no drilling, keep outlets clean).
